text: The first presentation we have is an update on the division's response to employee engagement and feedback. We're pleased to be able to provide you a comprehensive update on much of the work that's been underway for quite some time, and Mrs. Holly Coy is going to kick us off.

Great. Thank you. Good afternoon, Chair Shea, Vice Chair Irving, members of the board, and Dr. Cashwell. I am pleased to bring an update to you this afternoon on the work of the division to respond to the feedback we've been gathering from employees since last summer about contracts, compensation, and their levels of engagement as HCPS employees.

As a quick recap, there have been a number of inflection points in this work over the last year that have brought us to this update today. Last spring, the Board requested a comprehensive report that included information on collective bargaining in Virginia, as well as employee engagement in HCPS.

the summer, staff conducted research, created and deployed a new survey for all HCPS staff, and hosted focus groups to provide the board and division leaders with a timely and multi-layered analysis. A report was then provided to the board and the public in September, and in October the board shared their budget priorities developed in response, as well as requests for other responsive administrative actions. Today's presentation provides a progress report those requests and actions. As I noted in October, you clearly articulated spending

priorities and priorities related to policies and operations. Part of that statement is included here today and today's presentation provides updates on these items. Before proceeding to the progress update, I wanted to provide a quick overview of what we heard from employees last summer, which has been the foundation of the work and the request that you all made. As you recall, we focused on three major feedback mechanisms: the 2024 HCPS Annual Survey, a Summer 2024

Employee Engagement Survey, and the Summer 2024 Employee Focus Groups. Employees shared their feedback about what they most value about their employment in HCPS and areas where they see opportunities for improvement. Notably, many ranked highly their relationships with colleagues, opportunities for professional growth and wages. Others ranked contractual matters, including compensation and working conditions, along with recognition mechanisms as areas for improvement as a division. Some of the highlights from those surveys are provided here. However, I want to note that the detailed reports previously shared on each of these provide

nuanced feedback by employee type, which have also guided the work. In the summer 2024 survey, employees were asked to rank areas which they would like to change, with one being their highest priority. As you saw in the last slide, 60 percent of survey respondents selected their contract as the thing they would most like to change about their employment. This graph shows how all employee groups rank different areas they would like to change. Drilling in a bit further, this graph illustrates what the survey respondents meant by contracts. Over 60 percent of the survey

respondents who selected contracts as the priority area for improvement they were asked which topics within that were of the greatest concern compensation which was defined as wages salary and or pay for extra duties or coverage was the clear priority followed by benefits such as health insurance and retirement benefits leave policies planning time and work hours also receive significant attention Outside of contracts, 22% of employees cited the work environment and resources as the next highest priority area for change.

This graph illustrates what respondents meant by work environment and resources in greater detail. So, based on that and the more nuanced feedback behind it that was gathered and presented by staff, the board shared their overarching budget priorities and made a request for specific administrative actions to respond to that employee feedback.

At that time, the Board announced their budget priority for the coming year as raises for all staff, specific market adjustments for certain employee groups such as instructional assistants and custodial and maintenance teams. Second, you noted the capital improvement increases to support roofing, mechanical and transportation needs.

And third, the expansion of the Opportunity School Model to support schools with higher rates of teacher turnover and provisionally licensed staff. Additionally, you requested internal work begin to address employee concerns as noted in the lighter blue boxes here. As HCPS leaders have dug into these topics further, we've done so in partnership with many different advisory committees, work groups, and regularly scheduled convenings of various employee groups. Some of these are long-standing groups, some have existed for a bit

but were redesigned this year, and others were created new this year, but they all share common purpose in ensuring that employees from many different parts of the organization have the opportunity to surface issues and shape the solutions to shared challenges. One example of a redesigned advisory committee is the superintendent's teacher advisory committee. This year, the membership of the group was expanded with the number of representatives from each building going up to three as a maximum. And with more representation from each building, we have sought

to strengthen communication flow in both directions. Additionally, this year a steering committee made up of the Teacher of the Year finalists from each magisterial district was created for the first time to guide the work of the larger group. The format of the monthly meetings has been restructured to center employee concerns and hot topics, and public meeting summaries are created by staff so that teachers can easily share back updates at their buildings.

This redesign continues to be an evolving work in progress, refined and shaped by the feedback provided by teachers both on and off the committee about how it can be most effective. So where has all this input gone, and what has it turned into?

First and foremost, employee input has informed the budget recommendations of the superintendent and the school board. At the board's last monthly meeting, a recommended financial plan was approved, which is directly responsive to the feedback employees provided. It prioritizes significant pay raises, invests in planning time and professional learning, and elevates staff recognition efforts in every school in the county by providing funding to each and every school for that purpose. It also transforms an existing central position to support that work and employee recognitions division-wide.

Furthermore, the budget responds directly to employee requests for improved working conditions with targeted investments in staff support, including more English learner teachers, counselors, and SSOs.

It includes raises for custodial and maintenance staff, which were designed to better recruit and retain our essential personnel, and our capital improvement requests reflect those building needs as well. The budget also included funds to expand the Opportunity School model, including its compensation incentives and additional staff support for Ratcliffe Elementary and Brooklyn Middle beginning in the fall of 2025. Finally, the capital improvement plan proposed this year reflects the need for increased investments in roofing, mechanical, to include HVAC, and all part of improving our physical infrastructure that is both a working environment for our staff

and learning environment for our students. Additionally, one of the administrative requests was to look into automated timekeeping for HCPS employees. Staff explored numerous add-on systems and those conversations converged with a new pilot underway for redesigned staff ids in hcps it is possible that the pilot that the new staff ids may integrate with timekeeping systems but we will be evaluating that as the pilot concludes at the end of the school year as was

noted earlier a great deal of feedback was provided by employees about expectations and compensation for their time so since the summer staff have been digging into this topic with various employee groups to identify more specific areas of concern and brainstorm ways in which clarity and/or change can be provided.

A new working group was created on the topic and the issues have been surfaced among many of our other existing advisories and committees, namely our Teacher Advisory Committee. As a result of these conversations, staff have drafted a new document to help provide clarity on frequently cited topics called a contract addendum.

This document will be attached to our continuing and probationary teacher contracts which are issued in May. The document will provide plain language clarity on things such as expectations for after-school events and a breakdown of the days and hours in a teacher's contract. Staff has also worked on proposed revisions to 14 corresponding policies, which we anticipate coming before the board for first review on March 27th. These policies touch on everything from contracts to professional learning expectations to planning time and duties.

Finally, these conversations have included feedback on changes to the leave policy for our staff. Those discussions are ongoing and staff is continuing to work on some potential options for board consideration later this spring. In addition to taking action with redesigned advisories, contract addendums, and policy changes, we continuously evaluate and see feedback on how our communications can be as clear and efficient as possible.

This year, we developed a new page on the website dedicated to the budget process and information about how HCPS spends its money. Additionally, we are continuing conversations with teachers about how we communicate information about the pay scale given our unique model and how we can communicate the clarity provided in the contract addendum.

We also continue to use all our regular communication channels to keep our HCPS staff informed and apprised of developments. I want to close the presentation with some words from one of our employees who participated in a focus group last summer.

They're always trying to grow something and make it better. We're always changing, but I know that change is trying to make it better as well. So while you've heard a progress update on specific actions and items today, the conversations are ongoing and the commitment to meaningful and impactful employee feedback is widespread as an organization.
